headline: Zscaler chief executive Jay Chaudhry said fears that AI will wipe out software companies are overblown and that AI makes cybersecurity more necessary.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a company CEO defending his own business, partly promotional.
importance_line: Investors in software and security stocks get a counter-view to the 'SaaSpocalypse' fear, but Chaudhry runs a company with an interest in the answer, and its shares are down over 8% this year.
summary: Zscaler chief executive Jay Chaudhry told CNBC on 6 Oct 2026, as relayed by Stocktwits, that talk of a "SaaSpocalypse", meaning AI replacing software firms, is overblown and that "cyber is not keeping up" with fast-moving AI models. He added that AI agents will be "probably far more dangerous" weak links than human users, while the company reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of about $3.9 billion.
notes: Yahoo Finance carries a Stocktwits article ('originally published on StockTwits'); credited to Stocktwits, with CNBC as the interview source. Stocktwits URL not known; Yahoo link used.
